text:
mira: noticed apiserver FD count creeping on eu-west1, watch fanout >> normal. controllers start queuing and gpu-onboard jobs stuck in provisioning. anybody else seeing this?
sam: yep saw alerts around +07:12 UTC. apiserver pods on node-group-a at 98% FD.
jonathan: logs show a lot of long-lived watches from metrics-exporter and a custom billing-agg controller.
lina: billing-agg was rolled out yesterday with a bug that re-registers watches on reconcile loop. rolling back now.
mira: copying top lines from apiserver proc status to chat:
```
FDs: 8192/32768
netstat -an | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l -> 6200
kubectl get --raw /api/v1/watch... slow responses
apiserver: watch-cache items open: 78k, watchers: 4.3k
```
sam: that watcher count is nuts. etcd read latency is also up: etcd p99 reads 420ms -> timeouts on some controller retries.
ops-bot: alert: apiserver-fd-usage-high (eu-west1) -> 95%
jonathan: controller-manager shows backoff loops for Deployments and GPUProvision CRs, failing to progress. GPU attach jobs WAITING because kubelet can't update status.
lina: rollback completed for billing-agg, but watchers aren't dropping immediately. any ideas for mitigation?
mira: we can temporarily scale apiserver to extra replicas in eu-west1 to spread fds, and bump ulimit on apiserver nodes. also add short-term service eviction for the metrics-exporter via NetworkPolicy to force disconnect.
sam: agree. propose: 1) cordon one apiserver node and restart pods with increased --max-requests-inflight? 2) increment fd soft limit from 8192 -> 16384 on controlplane AMI 3) remove long-polling client if still present.
jonathan: do we have a way to force drop stale watches without full restart? maybe touch watch-cache TTL?
mira: no safe API for that. watch-cache gets cleaned when clients disconnect or when resource versions move beyond TTL. restart is fastest.
lina: rolling restart now on apiserver nodes A and B, will do one at a time. watching watch count.
(5m)
mira: watch count dropped from 4.3k -> 900 after first restart, etcd p99 read down to 110ms. GPUProvision CRs started processing again but a few attach ops remain pending.
sam: can we throttle the controller-manager retries to ease pressure? adjust --controllers flags? or patch backoff config.
jonathan: patched controller-manager to increase initial backoff from 250ms -> 1s and cap retries. that reduced hot loops.
lina: second apiserver restart done. fd usage stable at ~28%.
mira: propose followups: - run a job to scan for controllers re-registering watches (add tracing) - temp rate-limit heavy watchers at API layer - add runbook step: restart apiserver pod if fds > 80% - consider watch coalescing feature for apiserver (longer batch window)
sam: also need a postmortem to track cost impact: extra apiserver replicas and restarts increased infra churn and delayed GPU onboarding by ~12m per customer. I'll capture cost delta.
jonathan: will open a ticket for billing-agg PR fix and add e2e for watch cleanup.
lina: can we add a synthetic test that opens lots of watches to detect leaks pre-prod?
mira: yes, add to chaos suite.
ops-bot: deployment: apiserver-restart-euw completed by lina. incident -> monitoring resumed.
(final)
mira: thanks all. short-term mitigations worked. assigning owners: jonathan -> root cause fix for billing-agg, sam -> cost writeup, lina -> runbook entry. reopening if anything flares back up.
